result:
T-DG7-DO-A is not complete: the release tools are built, but two of the eleven required tests fail, T-A5 (build from the archive) and T-A11 (scan of the real built tree). Both failures come from defects in `deploy/scripts/assemble-runtime.sh`, which I'm not allowed to edit and which predates this task. Everything else in the assignment exists and its tests pass, except `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, which this sandbox would not let me write. Nothing is committed; the handback is `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG7/T-DG7-DO-A-devops-engineer.md`, with logs in `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG7/T-DG7-DO-A-evidence/`.

**Test results** (Node 24.21.0, `node --test tools/release/tests/*.test.mjs licenses/tests/*.test.mjs`):
- **Pass:** T-A1, T-A2, T-A3 (GNU tar), T-A4, T-A6, T-A7, T-A8, T-A9, T-A10.
- **Not run:** the bsdtar half of T-A3, because bsdtar isn't installed.
- **Full run:** 58 tests, 55 pass, 2 fail (T-A5, T-A11), 1 skipped; exit 1.
- **Repeat runs** (locale unset and `C.UTF-8`, without the T-A5/T-A11 inputs): 55 pass, 0 fail, 3 skipped. The two tests skip with a BLOCKED reason and are not counted as passes.

**Why T-A5 and T-A11 fail:**
- **T-A5 (proposed High, deployment portability).** At line 128, `assemble-runtime.sh` turns `string_decoder@1.1.1` into `string`, so its layout check refuses the runtime tree. The Dockerfile (line 59) and `clean-start-local.sh` (line 123) call the same script, so the image build and the clean start would fail the same way. Inside the network namespace, everything before that step worked:
  - both network probes failed, as required;
  - the offline install passed in 1.2 s;
  - `pnpm -r build` passed in 119.1 s.

  I propose a one-line fix in the handback; I tested the regex on sample names but not in the script.
- **T-A11 (proposed Medium).** The scan finds 48 hits, all the path the runtime tree was assembled in, recorded in pnpm's own metadata (`.modules.yaml`, `.pnpm-workspace-state-v1.json`, `.bin` shims). All other built output and every third-party file is clean, and every allow-list entry is used. The fix is either to remove those files in `assemble-runtime.sh` or for you to decide they are out of scope for the scan.

**Rehearsal archive** (built with the synthetic fixture demo data, so a rehearsal, not a release):
- `mth-transformation-hub-0.1.0-a9679ce70fd7-REHEARSAL.tar.gz`, 12,669,468 bytes, 3004 files, built in 12.35 s.
- Archive SHA-256 `0dcc0c18…e2c5`; candidate `sha256:a9679ce7…de3f`.
- `--verify` passed all 7 checks (exit 0).
- It was built from a throwaway clone under `$TMPDIR` (commit `a51f3a8f`, HEAD plus my working tree), because the new tools are uncommitted. The repository's `.git` was not touched.

**Other checks:**

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `generate-sbom --check` | exit 0; 483 packages: 426 not_required, 57 review, 0 required |
| `service-list --check` | exit 0 |
| `check-ci-needs` on `deploy/ci/ci.yml` | exit 0; new `release` job |
| `pnpm lint` | exit 0 |
| repository-wide Prettier check | exit 0 |
| `validate.mjs --historical --stage DG6` | exit 0 |

**Environment facts:**
- No Docker daemon, and no live CI run (D-058).
- The shell's default `node` is 22.22.0; every check used 24.21.0.
- The host pnpm store is read-only to this run and pnpm needs a writable one, so the builds used a copy.
- My first full clone filled the disk to 413 MB free. I deleted it and switched to clones that don't check files out.

**What you need to do:**
1. Run `cp deploy/ci/ci.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml`, then `node deploy/scripts/check-ci-needs.mjs`. The two files already differed at the starting commit (`cb02a91b`), so this also brings in DG6's CI changes.
2. Assign the two `assemble-runtime.sh` fixes, then rerun T-A5 and T-A11.
3. Run the container halves on your host: the image build and `compose up` from the archive. They will hit the same `assemble-runtime.sh` failure until it is fixed.

The handback lists 11 deviations, each with its reason, and 4 open questions. Two to note: the archive manifest records the Node version, which conflicts with the ADR's claim that the uncompressed archive bytes are identical on any platform; and the web app ships source maps.
